rationale: C12 is a concrete and material template for the child. It concerns the same Fort Armstrong lands at Kaakaukukui, the same Honolulu Harbor improvement project, and the same transfer of possession, use, control, and title to the Territory of Hawaii. Most distinctively, both directives make the transfer effective only after Hawaii completes replacement or alteration work at its own expense and the responsible federal agency certifies satisfactory completion. C13 uses closely parallel conditional-transfer machinery for an adjacent harbor-improvement tract, while C09 shares the restoration-and-title-transfer formulation but lacks the child's distinctive agreement, construction, and certification mechanism.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Fort Armstrong Military Reservation at Kaakaukukui, Honolulu, Oahu, Territory of Hawaii ... reserved for naval and military purposes ... by Presidential Proclamation dated November 10, 1899, and a series of Executive orders enumerated in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of November 14, 1930
shared_material.parent_excerpt: a tract of land at Kaakaukukui, Honolulu, Oahu, Territory of Hawaii ... was reserved for military purposes by a series of Executive orders (enumerated in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of November 14, 1930) describing the Fort Armstrong Military Reservation
shared_material.explanation: The directives identify the same reservation, location, provenance, and enumerating prior order in closely parallel language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: is needed by the Territory of Hawaii for purposes of an improvement project in Honolulu Harbor
shared_material.parent_excerpt: is needed by the Territory of Hawaii for a harbor-improvement project
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same factual predicate for returning Fort Armstrong property to Hawaii.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the following-described lands ... shall be restored to the possession and use of the Territory of Hawaii, and title thereto shall be transferred to the Territory
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the possession, use, and control of the two following-described tracts ... shall be restored to the Territory of Hawaii, and title to the said tracts shall be transferred to the said Territory
shared_material.explanation: The operative grant closely reproduces C12's combined restoration-and-title-transfer formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: subject to the condition that the Territory shall fully comply with the terms of its agreement ... and shall become effective only upon the certification by a designated representative of the General Services Administration that the work described therein has been satisfactorily completed
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Upon the fulfillment of the conditions precedent specified in Part II of this order and the certification thereof by the Department of the Army ... the possession, use, and control ... shall be restored ... and title ... transferred
shared_material.explanation: Both employ the distinctive machinery of a conditional land transfer triggered by completion of construction or alteration work and federal certification.
